title: Investigate & remediate intermittent 5xx spikes from connection resets during model warmup bursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customer N reported sustained 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts during daytime traffic bursts starting 2026-03-09. Symptoms: short-lived waves of 502/504 and connection resets observed in the hosted API proxies that correlate with many small streaming requests arriving simultaneously for large-context models that trigger model warmup and worker spin-up. SDK clients then retried aggressively (default policy), amplifying the surge and producing tenant-visible error spikes.

Hypothesis / Root cause (current):
- Runtime worker warmup path evicts or restarts worker processes when many unique model contexts are requested concurrently, causing upstream sockets to be closed mid-request (connection reset) and the edge proxy to surface 502/504.
- The edge and internal proxies have aggressive short idle timeouts and conservative keepalive limits; many short-lived streaming connections prevent TCP/TLS session reuse.
- Client SDKs default retry behavior (3 retries with short backoff) combined with connection resets produced a retry amplification loop for affected tenants.
- Lack of a tenant-scoped circuit breaker and no idempotency token enforcement for streaming calls allowed retries to re-fanout to runtime and overload warmup queues.

Evidence collected so far:
- Grafana dashboard snapshots: spike in connection_reset_count (proxy->runtime) at 2026-03-09 11:42 UTC coincident with increased model_compile_ms metrics on runtime nodes. (link below)
- Runtime logs: worker PID churn + OOM-inflated memory pressure on warmup threads; stack traces show warmup path holding exclusive model file locks for several seconds.
- Proxy traces: large proportion of upstream errors are ECONNRESET during TLS handshake/early write.
- Customer-reported SDK traces show retries happening immediately after the first failure with no idempotency header present.

Immediate mitigations (already enacted):
- Temporarily lowered SDK default retries for onboarding customers (support sent configuration snippet to Customer N to disable client retries for affected routes).
- Increased proxy keepalive to 60s in region eu-west-1 and bumped connection pool limits for the internal proxy to reduce churn (hotfix rolled 2026-03-10).
- Applied a soft rate cap on warmup-heavy model families via routing policy that falls back to a pre-warmed, lower-capacity variant to limit new warmups until runtime patch lands.

Proposed permanent fixes (plan):
1) Runtime warmup queueing and backpressure (core):
   - Make warmup path async and bounded: accept request, return queued token and continue streaming partial fallback response rather than blocking worker allocation.
   - Add per-model warmup concurrency limits and cooperative queuing across parent processes to avoid mass worker restarts.
2) Connection resilience (infra):
   - Enable TCP/TLS session reuse and increase keepalive defaults across proxies and runtime gateways.
   - Tune upstream idle and handshake timeouts to avoid early connection resets during warmup.
3) Idempotency + retry controls (API/clients):
   - Introduce an optional Idempotency-Token header for streaming/generation endpoints; if present, upstream will deduplicate in-flight warmup/retry attempts.
   - Update SDK defaults to backoff-jittered retries and expose tenant-level configuration for retry ceilings.
4) Tenant-scoped circuit breakers & cooling (platform):
   - Per-tenant short-term circuit (5xx rate) that returns controlled 429/503 with Retry-After when warmup overload is detected, plus a tenancy-specific cooldown window.
   - Admin API to temporarily throttle aggressive tenants during escalations.
5) Observability & runbooks (ops):
   - New dashboard panels for warmup_queue_depth, model_warmup_latency_ms, connection_reset_rate, and retry_amplification_index.
   - Playbook entry for customer-facing mitigation steps and comms templates.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Create unit + integration tests for warmup queue behavior and idempotency dedupe.
- Canary rollout of runtime warmup changes to staging and a single region (us-east-1) with traffic shaping for 48h. Monitor connection_reset_rate and tail latency.
- Gradual global rollout with feature flag; hold rollback thresholds: >2x baseline 5xx rate or >15% p50 latency increase.

Customer communications and escalations:
- Support drafted targeted message for Customer N explaining temporary controls already applied and expected timeline for patches (link to draft in Confluence).
- Offer dedicated tenant throttle window and one-on-one runbook with SE team to tune retry config in customer SDKs.

Open tasks (next 7 days):
- ENG: runtime PR for bounded warmup queue (Markus) - in progress.
- INFRA: apply TLS reuse config to staging proxies and run soak (Priya) - blocked on cert rotation window.
- DX: SDK change to expose idempotency token and default retry reduction (Sofia) - draft PR ready.
- OPS: create warmup observability panels and alert rules (Liam) - planned.

Longer-term follow-ups (post-fix):
- Postmortem capturing metrics & customer impact breakdown, with lessons learned on idempotency and warmup semantics.
- Revisit model packaging to reduce cold-start duration and file lock contention.
